summary: Interim report (shift still running). FOUND: web-01's site plugin folder held a hand-copied file, inc/rental-quote.php (not in the git repo), with a hidden branch: a POST with a fixed 'ref' value returned the DB_* settings from wp-config.php, including the website's database password, and offered a password-check oracle. The access log shows that branch answered twice (247-byte replies): 107.77.41.23 on 4 Nov 14:53 UTC and 174.205.223.135 on 11 Nov 12:10 UTC. So the site's database password (wp_larkspur) was read by outsiders. I found no sign that they got further: the DB account only accepts office-network addresses, all SSH logins on the three servers match staff and their usual addresses, no web shell in uploads, no rogue keys, cron or sudo use; db-01 and ci-01 show no intruder activity. DONE: removed the hidden branch (normal quotes still work); rotated app-db-password with rotate-secret on web-01 and updated the second copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf (report, orders and payouts jobs verified ok). Weaknesses closed: removed the old 'Blue Ridge Support Tools' mu-plugin (unauthenticated shell command injection via ?asup=purge; never hit in the logs; copy in /root/quarantine); removed deploy's passwordless 'sudo rsync' (root for anyone with the deploy account; the release only needs larkspur-deploy); locked the jpark account on web-01 and ci-01 and deleted the jpark WordPress administrator (Jun Park is not in the staff directory, was in sudo on web-01, never logged in); nginx now refuses PHP under uploads/cache; larkspur-deploy chown no longer follows symlinks; internal maint.d steps no longer writable by the web user; WordPress file editor disabled; on ci-01 the repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable, now group-only; the backups key on ci-01 is limited to db-01's address. NOT changed: password SSH logins stay on because several staff have no key; Grafana (3000) and the node exporter (9100) still listen publicly. Not rotated: payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, root-only secrets, deploy password - no sign they were read.
